records.location: Ladywell Fields park, near Ladywell railway station, Lewisham, southeast London SE13; old toilet block not precisely established.

records.name: Moat Mount Layby
records.location: Moat Mount Open Space / historic layby, Barnet Way (A1 southbound), Mill Hill, north London EN5/NW7; no precise active layby pinned.
records.description: Barnet Council confirms Moat Mount woodland is southbound on the A1 and physically separated from Scratchwood by the dual carriageway. CruisingGays independently lists Moat Mount Parking Area but preserves a dated 18 June 2008 visitor report that the carpark was already closed for parking then. This historic closure is not verified as still in force in 2026; do not imply active layby or recent encounter.
records.original_source_description: Lorries park beside the road. Woods with some open areas. It is a picnic spot further up, so don't bother if it is a sunny weekend or holiday. Just wander up and down the trails. Cruisiest spot in the woods alongside the park during the day.

records.name: Scratchwood

records.description: Barnet Council confirms Scratchwood's ancient woodland, nature-reserve paths and A1 northbound entrance. A separate CruisingGays archive identifies Scratchwood, including visitor text dated 7 January 2009 describing vegetation clearance; there are no verified recent first-hand encounters. records.original_source_description: The wooded area between the car park and the A1. Large car park below cafe off A1 between Mill Hill and Borehamwood. Park up and walk into woods. Don't just sit in your car. Cruise along the main path. There are sunbathing areas in the woods.
